audit_notes: Parameter check: all positive and physical. The 20-year mean solar absorptance of 0.08 (SR 0.92) is optimistic for a porous white surface in a dusty hot climate; field data for BaSO4/porous cooling coatings show SR losses of 0.03-0.08 within 1-2 years from dust, so I raise it to 0.10 (SR 0.90 mean). Emittance 0.95 is plausible for BaSO4/silicate but alumina has a reststrahlen dip near 11-15 um; kept at 0.94. net_longwave_sky_loss 80 W/m2 for a horizontal roof at near-ambient surface temperature in a dry climate is plausible by day (60-100 W/m2); for vertical walls it would be ~20 W/m2 - this model represents the roof case. wall_conductance 0.526 W/m2K = 1/(1/0.5 - 1/20). Dimensionless: Biot number of the envelope Bi = wall_conductance/h_o = 0.026 (the outer surface is controlled by the external balance). Radiative fraction of absorbed load. Simulation coefficient: effective sol-air excess temperature of the design (alpha*I - eps*dR)/h_o = (60-75.2)/20 = -0.76 K, i.e. the roof surface runs slightly below air temperature; baseline (0.32*600-0.9*80)/20 = +6.0 K. Model: steady 1D conduction d2T/dx2=0 with Robin/flux outer boundary and fixed indoor temperature; linear, closed-form solution. Metric: heat flux to the room q = -wall_conductance*dT/dx at x=1. Baseline: aged conventional cool paint alpha=0.32, eps=0.90. Expected q_design = 0.526*(260+60-75.2)/20.526 = 6.27 W/m2 vs q_base = 0.526*(260+192-72)/20.526 = 9.74 W/m2 -> 35.6% (roof). Stress/material check: surface temperature ~37-38 C; silicate/alumina coating far below any thermal limit; the porous network's mechanical weakness (abrasion by sand) is a durability, not a safety, issue. Audit passed.
